newsitem.title: CHINA: Troubled China Peugeot lowers prices of spares.
newsitem.headline: Troubled China Peugeot lowers prices of spares.

text.p: Troubled Sino-French car venture Guangzhou Peugeot Automobile has lowered the price of its spare parts by an average of 20 percent, a company official said on Wednesday.
Guangzhou Peugeot, 30 percent owned by French firm Peugeot Automobiles, ordered the cuts after many car owners complained that spares and repairs were too expensive, a company official said.
"We've resolved to lower parts prices by 20 percent," the official said. "This way, we'll have about the same prices as parts for other brands of cars."
The venture, based in the city of Guangzhou, the capital of southern Guangdong province, had set maximum prices its retailers across the country could charge for parts, he said.
"Although that will make us take a bit of a loss, our total car sales will rise," he said.
A slumping domestic car market had also been factored into the joint venture's decision to cut prices, the official said.
"We have been affected, and affected in a big way," he added without elaborating.
Peugeot Automobile denied last week that it would quit the joint venture after French media reports that the project was on the brink of failure.
Guangzhou Peugeot stopped producing cars several months ago. The group's Citroen division runs a joint venture plant in China's central city of Wuhan.
South Korean automaker Hyundai Motor Co has applied to Chinese authorities for a 22 percent stake in the venture, Chinese media said last week.
French newspaper Le Monde said Hyundai, Opel and Bayerische Motoren Werke AG (BMW) were lined up to take Peugeot's place if it abandoned the project.
The China Daily Business Weekly said Hyundai's application for a stake had heated up competition among rivals Honda Motor Co, Ford Motor Co and BMW which are all interested in a role.
